elements.label: Figure 6.7
elements.description:
Twelve small choropleth maps of Vietnam's districts ("Poverty and environmental risk maps"), each showing only districts ranking in the top third of one environmental variable, with districts coloured by poverty category. Legend (right side): three columns labelled Low poverty, Medium poverty and High poverty, and three rows. Row 1, "Environmental risk (top third)": yellow swatch (under Low poverty), red-brown swatch (under Medium poverty), dark navy swatch (under High poverty). Row 2, "Medium": dark teal swatch (under High poverty). Row 3, "Low": steel-blue swatch (under High poverty). Map panels, row by row:

Row 1: (a) Mean flood depth: mostly blue districts in the north and along the central coast; yellow and orange-brown clusters in the northeast and the southern Mekong delta coast. (b) Average slope: dark navy districts dominate the northern mountains; red and yellow districts appear along the northeast border and a narrow central strip. (c) Average PM2.5: yellow top-third districts cluster in the northern midlands around the Red River area; the central and southern areas are steel blue (low).

Row 2: (d) Variation in precipitation: red and yellow districts run along the central and south-central coast; northwest areas are mostly light blue. (e) Variation in wind speed: yellow and red districts sit along the north and central coast and the southern tip. (f) Variation in temperature: yellow districts concentrate in the northern midlands; the south is mostly teal and light blue. (g) Variance drought: orange and yellow districts run along the central coast and in the far south; the north and central highlands are mixed navy and light blue.

Row 3: (h) Average percipitation: red districts form a band along the central coast and the southern delta, with dark navy districts inland. (i) Mean wind speed: yellow districts cluster in the northeast near the border; red districts sit in the far south and along the central coast. (j) Mean temperature: red and yellow districts are concentrated in the southern delta; the north is mostly steel blue. (k) Mean drought: yellow and red districts cluster in the northeast and north-central areas and in the southern delta; the northwest is dark navy and the central coast is light blue.

Note printed below the figure: only districts ranking in the top third of the environmental variable are shown; poverty rates are grouped into high, medium and low categories by ranking of district-level poverty rates (see Table 6.1). Source: World Bank staff calculations. Basemap credit: ©Mapbox ©OSM. Overall pattern: the highest-risk districts are concentrated in the northern midlands and mountains, the central coast and the Mekong delta, with the Mekong delta and northern provinces showing the most overlap of high-risk variables.
